summary: Five distinct organisms with primary or authoritative global research; staged importable batch because direct publishing workflow is not presently passing subsequent ingestions. Primary ethnographic corroboration remains pending for culantro culinary attribution.
research_method: Cross-checked Reports 004–011 and current canonical GitHub taxa; region-specific primary studies and public EMA, Chinese, Cuban, Japanese and Korean sources. Evidence tiers separate human, preclinical, traditional and analytical claims.

organisms.geographic_context: China, Korea, Japan; Chinese materia medica
organisms.part_and_preparation_note: Fruit (qingqiao immature green; laoqiao mature yellow); glycoside composition varies with ripening
organisms.research_notes: Forsythiaside A is a phenylethanoid glycoside; phillyrin is a lignan glycoside. Antiviral and anti-inflammatory reports largely in vitro/animals; no demonstrated clinical infection cure.

organisms.part_and_preparation_note: Fruit/achenes; silymarin is a mixture, not a molecule; standardized extracts differ from seed tea
organisms.research_notes: Clinical reviews report uncertain patient-important benefits; some liver enzyme outcomes vary. Silybin A/B are distinct stereoisomers.

organisms.part_and_preparation_note: Dried tuber; alkaloid proportions and enantiomers vary
organisms.research_notes: Isocorypalmine bound dopamine D1 receptors in an assay (Ki 83 nM); in vivo pain models do not prove human pain treatment.

organisms.geographic_context: Caribbean and tropical America; cultivated in Southeast Asia
organisms.part_and_preparation_note: Leaves for food versus seeds for volatile-oil analyses; compositions not interchangeable
organisms.research_notes: Cuban seed-oil GC-MS found carotol 19–31% and other terpenes; culinary uses are not evidence of therapeutic action.

organisms.geographic_context: Japan and Korea; pine-associated edible ectomycorrhizal fungus
organisms.part_and_preparation_note: Fruiting body; cap vs stalk and storage change flavor chemistry
organisms.research_notes: Japanese and Korean studies measured volatile flavor compounds, amino acids and 5-prime nucleotides; no clinical cognitive or immune outcome established.

safety.alert: Human dosing, pregnancy safety, drug interactions and extract-specific toxicity are insufficiently established; in-vitro antiviral results are not treatment instructions.
Asteraceae allergy and gastrointestinal effects possible; EMA traditional monograph is not evidence for serious liver-disease treatment.
Sedation, dopamine-related interactions and possible cardiac sodium-channel effects warrant caution; avoid treating animal doses as human doses.
Culinary leaves are not equivalent to concentrated seed essential oil; high-concentration safety is not established.
